- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is flat or rising slowly, adjust upward by 1–3% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.  
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >5% from prior period), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% per subsequent period to avoid overshoot.  
- If official supply net is negative and sentiment is bearish (≤0.33), model often underestimates downside; add 1–2% downward bias to forecast mean.  
- When sentiment swings from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model fails to adjust; apply a 0.5–1.0% downward correction to forecast starting 2–3 days after sentiment shift.  
- In high-event periods (≥15 events/30d), model tends to overestimate price rise; cap forecast growth at 0.5% per day unless sentiment is strongly bullish.  
- If true outcome deviates >5% from 30d forecast mean, check sentiment history for recent volatility; if sentiment was neutral or bearish, apply mean reversion to forecast by 1–2% per day.
